facts.fact_text: The applicant is a member of the Human Rights Association in Turkey.
At 8 p.m. on 8 April 2002, around 30-35 persons gathered at Tünel Square holding candles, photos and banners.
The demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 sat down on the street.

The applicant submitted in the application form that on 8 April 2002 he had arrived at Tünel Square in order to participate in the Human Rights Association's press release on Israel's invasion of Palestine.
The police used force to arrest the two persons, including the applicant, who continued to sit and shout slogans at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002.
The applicant submitted that the police then arrested him and Ms M.A.
The Beyoğlu public prosecutor considered in his decision of 7 August 2003 that the force used by the security forces was in line with Article 24 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

The police opened a passage for the demonstrators to leave Tünel Square on 8 April 2002.
The group of demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 started to disperse.
Two persons, including the applicant, continued to sit and shout slogans at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 despite warnings from the police.
The police used force to arrest the two persons, including the applicant, who continued to sit and shout slogans at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002.
In his decision of 7 August 2003, the Beyoğlu public prosecutor noted that following warnings from the police, the demonstrators had started to disperse on 8 April 2002.

In his decision of 7 August 2003, the Beyoğlu public prosecutor noted that the complainants had continued to sit down and shout slogans after warnings to disperse on 8 April 2002, and as a result the police had had to use force and arrest them.

On 10 June 2002 an Istanbul deputy police chief was appointed to carry out a preliminary investigation on behalf of the governor of Istanbul into the allegations of ill-treatment made by the applicant and Ms M.A.

The Istanbul deputy police chief's report recommended that authorisation for the prosecution of Mr Ş.P., the police chief on duty on 8 April 2002, should be declined on the ground that the complaints were ill-founded.

On 4 July 2002 the Istanbul Deputy Governor refused authorisation for the prosecution of Mr Ş.P., the police chief on duty on 8 April 2002, on the basis of the information contained in the Istanbul deputy police chief's report and statements.
On 26 November 2002 the Istanbul Regional Administrative Court upheld the applicant's objection on account of an insufficient investigation, notably regarding the other police officers involved.

On 7 March 2003 the Istanbul Governor declined authorisation for the prosecution of the police officers on the basis of the information contained in the second report and statements prepared by the Istanbul deputy police chief.
On 7 August 2003 the Beyoğlu public prosecutor decided not to prosecute the accused police officers.
